sections.h1Accent: Gulf-Ready Online Stores for Retailers and B2B Sellers

body.text: Teknoppy is a Magento development company GCC retailers, distributors and brands hire to build, upgrade and support Magento and Adobe Commerce stores for Gulf shoppers. Our in-house team in Kochi, India, works on Gulf hours and builds Arabic and English stores with local payments, VAT rules and multi-country setups for the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain.

sections.trustline: Reviewed by Sanal Edison, Founder, Teknoppy. Last updated: 17 November 2026.

items.text: Team: Teknoppy, 12 in-house staff in Kochi, Kerala, since 2018
Gulf clients: businesses in Dubai, Sharjah, Doha, Dammam and Kuwait, including online retailers
Services: Magento builds, Adobe Commerce, B2B stores, local payments, VAT setup, upgrades and support
Time difference: 1.5 hours ahead of the UAE and Oman, 2.5 hours ahead of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain
Typical timeline: 10 to 20 weeks for a new store

paragraphs.text: Gulf ecommerce brings its own requirements: Arabic and English storefronts, several currencies, cash on delivery, buy-now-pay-later options, different VAT rates by country and fast delivery expectations. Magento handles large catalogues, multiple store views and complex pricing, which makes it a strong choice for retailers and distributors selling across the region. Its open architecture also connects well with ERPs, warehouses and marketplaces common in the Gulf.

Offshore Magento development for GCC retailers gives you an experienced, in-house team at Kerala rates, with a working day that overlaps your own. As a Magento development company GCC brands reach by video call, we report progress after every sprint and keep all code in repositories you own.

items.title: Magento Arabic English Store Setup
items.text: A Magento Arabic English store uses separate store views for each language, with right-to-left layouts for Arabic, translated product content, Arabic search and correct currency and number formats. Customers can switch languages without losing their cart. Product feeds for marketplaces and ads can also be generated in both languages.

items.title: Magento Multi-Country Store for the GCC
items.text: A Magento multi-country store GCC retailers run from one admin can serve the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain with their own currencies, prices, shipping rules, payment methods and tax settings. Stock can be shared or split by warehouse, and each country can show its own promotions, banners and featured products.

items.title: Tabby and Tamara Integration for Magento
items.text: Tabby and Tamara integration in Magento adds buy-now-pay-later options that many Gulf shoppers expect, letting customers split payments into instalments at checkout. Our Tabby and Tamara integration Magento work covers checkout display, product page messaging, order status updates and refunds, tested end to end before launch.

items.title: mada Payment Integration in Magento
items.text: Our mada payment integration Magento projects let Saudi shoppers pay with mada debit cards, alongside credit cards, Apple Pay and regional gateways. We also connect Kuwait's KNET, Qatar's local card networks and other payment providers your markets require. Every gateway is tested with real transactions in a sandbox before launch, including refunds and failed payments.

items.title: Magento VAT Setup for the UAE and Saudi Arabia
items.text: Magento VAT setup UAE and Saudi stores need applies VAT at 5% in the UAE and 15% in Saudi Arabia, displays tax correctly on product pages and invoices, and produces VAT reports for each filing period. Rates for Oman, Bahrain and other markets are configured per store view, while Qatar and Kuwait can run without VAT.

items.title: Magento B2B Store for the UAE and Gulf
items.text: A Magento B2B store UAE distributors and wholesalers use offers company accounts, customer-specific prices, quick order by SKU, quote requests and credit terms. Trade buyers reorder in minutes, and sales teams spend less time on phone orders. Each buyer sees only their own catalogue, prices and order history after logging in.

items.title: Adobe Commerce Development for the UAE
items.text: Adobe Commerce development UAE retailers choose suits larger brands that need Adobe's advanced B2B, marketing and content tools, cloud hosting and official support. We help you decide whether the paid edition is worth it before you commit, comparing licence costs against the features you would actually use.

items.title: United Arab Emirates
items.text: As a Magento development company UAE retailers work with remotely, we support businesses in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah. Brands looking for a Magento development company Dubai teams can call during office hours get the same in-house team for new stores, upgrades and support. Abu Dhabi and Sharjah retailers follow the same process, with demos scheduled inside UAE working hours. You can also hire Magento developers Dubai-focused on a monthly plan.

items.title: Saudi Arabia
items.text: Our Magento developers Saudi Arabia projects support retailers in Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam. As a Magento development company Riyadh brands can work with online, we build Arabic-first stores with mada, buy-now-pay-later options and Saudi VAT configured from day one.

items.title: Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain
items.text: Magento development Qatar clients book often supports retailers and distributors in Doha. Magento development Kuwait, Magento development Oman and Magento development Bahrain projects follow the same process, with local payments, delivery partners and tax settings planned during discovery and calls scheduled around local working weeks.

paragraphs.text: Magento support for GCC retailers covers security patches, extension updates, speed monitoring, backups and small improvements. Before peak seasons such as Ramadan, Eid, White Friday and national day sales, we load-test checkout, review caching and confirm payment and delivery integrations, so your store stays fast when traffic is highest. After each peak we review conversion and speed data and agree improvements for the next campaign.

As a Magento development company GCC sellers use for growth, we commonly build fashion and beauty stores with many variants, electronics and home appliance catalogues, building material and hardware stores with thousands of SKUs, and B2B portals for distributors that sell to retailers across several Gulf countries. Most share three needs: fast search, accurate stock and smooth bilingual checkout.

sections.h2: Why Teknoppy Is the Magento Development Company GCC Brands Shortlist

items.title: In-House Team
items.text: Every developer and designer on your store is employed by Teknoppy, with no subcontracting, so knowledge of your catalogue, extensions and integrations stays with one accountable team.

items.title: Gulf Ecommerce Experience
items.text: Teknoppy already works with businesses in the UAE, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, including online retailers. We understand bilingual product content, local payment habits, cash on delivery and regional delivery expectations, and we plan stores around how Gulf customers actually shop on mobile.

items.title: Proof and Accountability
items.text: Shainesh Prakashan, CEO of Exacore IT at Infopark Kochi, says Teknoppy "was very intuitive in understanding our requirements." Founder Sanal Edison reviews catalogue structure, search settings and integrations for every Gulf store before development begins.

items.title: What Gulf Clients Receive
items.text: Every project with our Magento development company GCC team includes a fixed written scope, a named project lead, weekly written updates, a staging store from the first sprint, full source code in your repository, and admin training for your ecommerce team, with Arabic user guides on request.

items.title: Discovery (1 to 2 weeks)
items.text: Video workshops on catalogue, markets, payments, delivery and integrations.

items.title: Design (2 to 3 weeks)
items.text: You approve English and Arabic designs for key pages and checkout.

items.title: Build sprints (2-week cycles)
items.text: Demos scheduled within Gulf working hours.

items.title: Data, payments and delivery (2 to 4 weeks, in parallel)
items.text: Product import, payment gateways and courier integrations.

items.title: Testing and launch (1 to 2 weeks)
items.text: Orders, payments, VAT, languages and speed are tested before go-live.

paragraphs.text: Typical totals: 10 to 14 weeks for a single-country retail store, and 14 to 20 weeks for a multi-country or B2B store. Adding a further Gulf country to an existing store usually takes 3 to 5 weeks.

sections.h2: Magento Development Cost in UAE and the Gulf

paragraphs.text: Magento development cost in UAE projects depends on catalogue size, number of countries and languages, payment and delivery integrations, B2B features and design complexity. How much does a Magento store cost in Dubai? Local agency quotes are high, which is why many Gulf retailers work with an experienced offshore team. Every Teknoppy project is quoted after discovery, with a fixed price for the agreed scope.

items.q: Can you take over our existing Magento store?
items.a: Yes. We begin with a code and security audit, share a written report, fix urgent issues first, then plan upgrades and improvements while your store keeps trading.

items.q: Do you support cash on delivery?
items.a: Yes. Cash on delivery can be enabled per country or region, with order limits, verification steps and courier integration to reduce failed deliveries.

items.q: Can you connect our store to Gulf delivery companies?
items.a: Yes. We integrate Magento with regional courier and last-mile delivery providers for shipping rates, label printing, tracking updates and delivery confirmations, so customers see accurate delivery times at checkout.

items.q: Do we own the store and its code?
items.a: Yes. You own the store, customer data and all custom code, with repository access and admin credentials handed over at launch.

items.q: How do I choose a Magento development company GCC retailers can trust?
items.a: Confirm the team is in-house, ask for live store examples, check how Arabic, local payments and VAT are handled, and insist on a fixed written scope.
